name: open_by_handle_at
synopsis: int open_by_handle_at(int mount_fd, struct file_handle *handle, int flags);
description: The open_by_handle_at() system call opens the file corresponding to a handle returned by a previous call to name_to_handle_at() and returns an open file descriptor. It uses a mount file descriptor, the file handle, and flags to perform the operation.

parameters.name: mount_fd
parameters.description: File descriptor for the mount point.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Pointer to the file handle structure obtained from name_to_handle_at().

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for opening the file, such as O_RDONLY or O_WRONLY.

return_value.success: Returns a file descriptor (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: mount_fd is not an open file descriptor.
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor (though this may not directly apply).
handle points outside your accessible address space.
handle->handle_bytes is greater than MAX_HANDLE_SZ or is equal to zero.
handle refers to a symbolic link, but O_PATH was not specified in flags.
The caller does not have the CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH capability.
The specified handle is not valid for opening a file, such as if the file has been deleted.
